\section{The unresolved exact-seven layer}\label{fin:sec:seven}

The theorem implies only \(\rho(H)\ge7\).  To distinguish this lower bound
from an exact value, we report bounded experiments at deletion budget seven.

In branch \(i\), the fixed unit \(\neg x_{f_i}\) accounts for one deletion
and an equality counter requires exactly six of the other \(826\) input edges
to be absent.  All \(4123\) original nonedges remain free.  The universal bank
of \(251771\) hitting clauses from branch \(0\) is valid in every branch and
was preloaded.  Every initial formula therefore had \(4950\) primary
variables, \(9840\) counter auxiliaries, \(161700\) triangle clauses,
\(19680\) counter clauses, one fixed unit, and \(251771\) hitting clauses, for
a total of \(433152\) clauses.

\begin{observation}[Bounded endpoints, not a theorem]
One solver call was launched per branch with a parent-enforced \(300\)-second
discovery wall.  Branch \(0\) used CaDiCaL, branch \(1\) Glucose~4.2, and
branch \(2\) MapleChrono.  Each remained inside its first SAT call until the
wall expired.  No branch produced a model that reached independent-set
separation, and no branch produced a checked refutation.  The endpoint of all
three branches is therefore \textsc{unknown}.
\end{observation}

The zero recorded separation iterations means that no SAT model returned
before interruption; it does not mean the formula is unsatisfiable.  The
recoverable state consists of the completely reconstructed initial formula
and universal cut bank.  Internal CDCL state was not serialized.  Exact
hashes of the frozen result and checkpoint records are listed in
\cref{fin:app:seven-record}.

\begin{proposition}[A degree-cap lift for branch~1]
Let \(F\) be triangle-free with \(\alpha(F)<18\).  Then
\(\deg_F(v)\le17\) for every vertex \(v\).  In branch~1, where
\((97,99)\) is fixed absent, every feasible set of six residual seed-edge
deletions contains an edge incident with vertex~\(98\).  Consequently this
condition alone excludes
\[
  \frac{\binom{808}{6}}{\binom{826}{6}}
  =0.875813014052041\ldots
\]
of the raw residual deletion sets.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The open neighbourhood of any vertex in a triangle-free graph is independent,
so its size is at most~\(17\).  After deleting the fixed branch edge
\((97,99)\), vertex~\(98\) still has seed degree~\(18\).  If \(D\) denotes
the six residual deletions and \(A\) the selected seed-nonedge additions, then
\[
  \deg_F(98)
  =18-|D\cap\delta(98)|+|A\cap\delta(98)|\le17.
\]
Thus \(D\) must meet the \(18\) residual seed edges incident with vertex~\(98\).
There are \(808\) residual edges not incident with \(98\), so precisely
\(\binom{808}{6}\) of the \(\binom{826}{6}\) raw six-edge sets are excluded.
\end{proof}

For the rest of this section put
\[
 E_1=E(H)\setminus\{(97,99)\},\qquad
 \Delta_{98}=\{e\in E_1:98\in e\}.
\]
Thus \(|E_1|=826\), \(|\Delta_{98}|=18\), and a branch-1 repair has a
residual deletion support \(D\in\binom{E_1}{6}\).

\begin{lemma}[Soundness of the branch-1 common relaxation]
\label{fin:lem:branch1-common-relaxation}
Let \(\Psi_1\) be the CNF consisting, in order, of all triangle clauses, an
exact-six counter on the literals \(\{\neg x_e:e\in E_1\}\), the unit
\(\neg x_{97,99}\), one degree-at-most-17 counter for every vertex, and the
ordered bank of \(251771\) universal independent-18 hitting clauses.  Every
feasible branch-1 exact-seven repair extends to a satisfying assignment of
\(\Psi_1\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The primary variables \(x_{uv}\) record the final graph.  Triangle-freeness
satisfies every triangle clause and the branch choice satisfies the fixed
unit.  Exactly six edges of \(E_1\) are absent, so the primary assignment has
an extension through the exact counter.  The degree-cap proposition gives an
extension through every degree counter.  Finally, for each stored 18-set
\(S\), the clause
\[
 \bigvee_{\{u,v\}\in\binom S2}x_{uv}
\]
is necessary when \(\alpha(F)<18\).  Hence every clause family is satisfied.
The bank need not contain every 18-set, so \(\Psi_1\) is a relaxation rather
than an exact encoding.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Four proof-checked singleton entailments]
\label{fin:prop:branch1-singleton-entailments}
Define
\[
 a=(11,62),\qquad b=(18,61),\qquad
 c=(18,64),\qquad d=(18,69).
\]
All four edges lie in \(E_1\setminus\Delta_{98}\).  The frozen relaxation
satisfies
\[
 \Psi_1\models x_a\wedge x_b\wedge x_c\wedge x_d.
\]
Thus none of these four seed edges can belong to the residual deletion support
of a feasible branch-1 repair.  No minimality assertion is made.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For each \(e\in\{a,b,c,d\}\), a standalone CaDiCaL run refuted
\[
 \Psi_1\wedge\neg x_e,
\]
and the pinned \texttt{drat-trim} checker accepted each emitted proof.  These
four checked refutations are equivalent to the displayed entailment by
\(\Psi_1\).  They are not asserted to be equivalent to the target-graph
statement; the necessary condition for target graphs follows only in the
forward direction from \cref{fin:lem:branch1-common-relaxation}.

Each DIMACS instance has \(154190\) variables and \(718453\) clauses.  A
PySAT-free checker that imports neither the production formula builder nor
the exporter reconstructed all four compressed CNFs byte for byte, including
the candidate-unit polarity.  A separately compiled checker binary on a
second architecture replayed all four proofs to the exact status
\texttt{s VERIFIED}.  The formula, proof, checker, and artifact identities are
recorded in \cref{fin:app:seven-record}.
\end{proof}

\begin{observation}[The common relaxation is nonempty]
A complete CaDiCaL model for \(\Psi_1\) was checked against an independent
byte-for-byte reconstruction of all \(718452\) clauses.  The model sets all
four displayed edge variables to true, as the proposition requires.  It also
contains the independent \(18\)-set
\[
 \{99,96,97,95,92,90,87,91,85,93,84,73,70,88,82,81,78,83\}.
\]
Hence the singleton entailments are not consequences of an empty common
relaxation, but this particular model is not an exact-seven Ramsey repair.
The satisfiability of \(\Psi_1\) resolves neither existence nor nonexistence
for the target problem because the universal bank is incomplete.
\end{observation}

\begin{corollary}[Support exclusion beyond the degree cap]
\label{fin:cor:branch1-singleton-count}
Every feasible branch-1 residual support \(D\) meets \(\Delta_{98}\) and
avoids \(\{a,b,c,d\}\).  The singleton no-goods exclude an additional
\[
 1307748575589
\]
supports beyond those already excluded by the degree cap.  Together the two
filters exclude
\[
 380670699850897
\]
of the \(\binom{826}{6}=433155188594590\) raw supports and leave
\(52484488743693\) outside these two necessary-condition filters.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The support restrictions follow from the degree-cap proposition,
\cref{fin:lem:branch1-common-relaxation}, and
\cref{fin:prop:branch1-singleton-entailments}.  Avoiding the four distinguished
edges leaves \(822\) eligible residual edges.  Because those four edges avoid
\(\Delta_{98}\), the supports that both avoid them and fail the degree test
are precisely the six-subsets of the other \(804\) nonincident edges.  Hence
the number surviving both filters is
\[
 \binom{822}{6}-\binom{804}{6}=52484488743693.
\]
Subtracting this from the degree-cap survivor count gives the additional
\(1307748575589\) exclusions.  Equivalently, the singleton clauses remove
about \(2.431110\%\) of the degree-cap survivors, and the combined filters
exclude about \(87.883214\%\) of the raw support universe.  These are
support-index counts, not a wall-time speedup or a count of graphs.
\end{proof}

The four retention units also permit a stricter audit of what follows from
the local triangle and degree systems before any new SAT call.  Propagating
those systems to the original nonedges gives exactly \(396\) forced-absent
addition variables: \(388\) come from pairs having more than six common
neighbours in the fixed branch base, two are forced by the retained-star
configuration, and six arise only from the coupled exact-six,
\(\delta(98)\), and degree constraints.  Substitution of all \(396\) units
into the finite \(I_{18}\) bank leaves no clause involving deletion variables
alone.  Thus this closure is useful preprocessing, but it supplies no new
deletion-support no-good beyond the filters proved above.

There is, however, a clean normal form that applies to the target problem
rather than merely to a finite bank.

\begin{proposition}[Maximal-triangle-free normal form]
\label{fin:prop:branch1-mtf-normal-form}
A feasible branch-1 exact-seven repair exists if and only if one exists that
is maximal triangle-free.  Equivalently, one may require every absent pair to
have a common neighbour.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Only the forward direction needs proof.  Starting from a feasible repair
\(F\), repeatedly add an absent pair \(uv\notin E(H)\) whenever \(u\) and
\(v\) have no common neighbour.  Such an addition creates no triangle,
cannot increase the independence number, and does not change
\(E(H)\setminus E(F)\).  The finite process terminates with the same exact
seven-edge deletion support and with every still-absent original nonedge
triangle-blocked.

It remains to consider an absent pair \(e\in E(H)\).  If \(e\) were safe to
add, doing so would again preserve triangle-freeness and could not increase
the independence number, while reducing the one-sided deletion count from
seven to six.  This contradicts the proof-checked theorem
\(\rho(H)\ge7\).  The argument also applies when \(e=(97,99)\): after adding
that fixed branch edge, at least one of the other two edges of the seed's
unique triangle remains absent, so the resulting graph is covered by the
global three-branch budget-six exclusion.  Hence every nonedge in the final
graph has a common neighbour, which is precisely maximal
triangle-freeness.  The reverse implication is immediate.
\end{proof}

This is an existence normal form, not a claim that every raw repair is
already maximal.  It is the fixed-support analogue of the standard use of
maximal triangle-free graphs in computational Ramsey searches
\cite{BrinkmannGoedgebeurSchlagePuchta2012}.  For a scoped pair \(uv\), an
exact existential CNF encoding introduces variables \(y_{uv,w}\) and uses

\[
 x_{uv}\vee\bigvee_{w\notin\{u,v\}}y_{uv,w},\qquad
 \neg y_{uv,w}\vee x_{uw},\qquad
 \neg y_{uv,w}\vee x_{vw}.
\]

Reverse implications are unnecessary: the \(y\)-variables only select one
common-neighbour witness when \(uv\) is absent.  Scoping this construction to
the \(4123\) original nonedges uses \(404054\) auxiliaries and \(812231\)
clauses; the full maximal-triangle-free encoding uses \(485100\) auxiliaries
and \(975150\) clauses.  A complete three-vertex truth-table audit checks the
existential semantics.

The two checked relaxation models illustrate the claim boundary.  The common
model has one unsafe original nonedge, \((37,86)\).  Adding it would create a
degree-\(18\) vertex, so the resulting graph is not asserted to remain a model
of the degree-capped incomplete-bank relaxation; the same pair instead
recovers the independent-\(18\) domination witness recorded below.  The A+
model has exactly three unsafe original nonedges,
\((16,64),(32,98),(40,89)\).  Adding all three gives a maximal triangle-free
primary graph with the same seven deletions and maximum degree \(17\), but it
still contains the already known independent set
\(\{81,82,\ldots,97,99\}\).  Maximality is therefore complementary to, not a
replacement for, independent-set separation.

Nor can a branch-1 conclusion be transferred by relabelling.  A deterministic
degree-initialized one-dimensional Weisfeiler--Leman refinement has \(3\),
\(15\), and \(100\) color classes at initialization, round one, and round two.
Every automorphism preserves every refinement color, so the singleton round
forces the automorphism group of the labelled seed to be trivial.  The other
two triangle-edge branches therefore require independent treatment.

For completeness, the domination diagnostic used above is the following
elementary consequence of the target conditions.  Put

\[
 Z_v=\{u\ne v:uv\notin E(F),\ N_F(u)\cap N_F(v)=\varnothing\}.
\]

Then \(N_F(v)\cup I\) is independent for every independent
\(I\subseteq F[Z_v]\), and hence
\(\alpha(F[Z_v])\le17-\deg_F(v)\).  In particular, degree \(17\) forces
\(Z_v=\varnothing\), while degree \(16\) forces \(Z_v\) to be a clique of
order at most two.  On the common model this exposes the new mask
\texttt{2000000404414192982822020}; it has zero overlap with the universal,
historical, A+, and fixed-base mask families.  On the A+ model it yields no
new mask, consistently with all three unsafe pairs having degree \(16\) at
both endpoints.  These are checked separators for relaxation models, not
new theorems about existence.

We encoded the same degree cap at both levels of a deletion-first branch-1
pilot.  The master selects six residual deletions and addition-eligibility
variables, separates conditional independent-set clauses, and passes a fixed
deletion set to an exact add-only subproblem.  An incomplete master separation
call may fall back to that exact subproblem.  If the fixed-deletion subproblem
is itself incomplete, the run stops without learning a deletion no-good.  A
completed fixed-deletion \textsc{unsat} may be used as solver-trusted search
telemetry, but it is not promoted without a checked proof trace.

\begin{observation}[Deletion-first endpoints, still not a theorem]
A six-configuration bounded matrix learned between zero and \(2816\) new
conditional independent-set cuts per run.  One MapleChrono configuration
reached two fixed-deletion \textsc{unsat} endpoints, but emitted no proof for
them; the same run then stopped at the independent-set oracle limit.  Three
predeclared positive-signal extensions raised that oracle limit from two
million to twenty million nodes.  Two stopped at exactly \(20{,}000{,}001\)
recursive nodes inside a fixed-deletion subproblem after learning \(10{,}780\)
and \(13{,}362\) new cuts, respectively; the third learned \(12{,}800\) cuts
but reached its \(300\)-second global wall before entering a subproblem.  No
run returned a verified candidate or a checked refutation.  Every endpoint
therefore remains \textsc{unknown}.
\end{observation}

The two apparent fixed-deletion separator stalls were then reconstructed under
an order-aware implementation.  The historical ascending recursion exhausted
its two-million-node allowance on both supports.  Reversing the vertex order,
which leaves the graph property unchanged, instead returned \(512\) validated
independent \(18\)-sets in \(11{,}261\) and \(10{,}057\) recursive nodes,
respectively, taking about \(0.006\) seconds in each case.  Thus the old
twenty-million-node endpoints were an ordering artefact on these supports,
not evidence of a combinatorial obstruction.

We consequently ran seven further bounded gates with a reverse-first,
bidirectional exact oracle.  On every master model for which separation was
invoked, a batch of either \(512\) or \(4096\) validated cuts was returned in
\(0.005\)--\(0.075\) seconds.  Nevertheless, each gate reached its global
wall after zero to five master models; none entered a fixed-deletion
subproblem, returned a verified candidate, emitted a proof, or learned a new
fixed-deletion no-good.  Under these particular checkpoints and limits, every
run reached its global wall while still in the master.  This remains bounded,
configuration-specific telemetry rather than a claim of intrinsic hardness.
The command lines, stable implementation hashes, all sixteen deletion-first
endpoints, and the stop rule are recorded in \cref{fin:app:seven-record}.

We also tested a genuinely different deletion-only projection.  It retains
the exact residual counter, local wedge implications for addition
eligibility, the complete \(235504\)-member fixed-base \(I_{18}\) covering
family, and the vertex-\(98\) hit constraint, while forgetting the full edge
assignment.  Its natural exact-six control has \(13159\) variables and
\(264757\) clauses.  A pinned CaDiCaL call reached its predeclared
\(300\)-second wall without a status line.  The incomplete proof prefix was
hashed and deleted, and the exact-seven instance was not run under the
predeclared stop rule.  This endpoint is \textsc{unknown}; more importantly,
the route failed its strength gate on an already known-unsatisfiable control
and therefore supplied no reason to spend a second long call.

Finally, a no-repeat A+ bank was generated from a checked common-relaxation
model after excluding the universal, historical, and exhaustive fixed-base
families.  Appending its \(4096\) new \(I_{18}\) clauses and the four proved
retention units produced a formula with \(154190\) variables and \(722552\)
clauses.  The single authorized solver call returned a complete satisfying
model after \(2532.362\) seconds.  An independent checker evaluated every
clause, recovered a triangle-free \(823\)-edge primary graph, and found the
independent \(18\)-set
\[
 \{81,82,83,84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,96,97,99\}.
\]
That set was absent from the installed universal and A+ banks but already
belonged to both the historical and exhaustive fixed-base families.  Thus A+
is a rigorously audited negative endpoint and, specifically, shows why a
fresh prefix is inferior to installing the complete deduplicated bank.  It
does not provide a repair or a branch refutation.

We therefore reconstructed that stronger bank explicitly.  The universal,
historical, and exhaustive fixed-base families contain \(251771\), \(64591\),
and \(235504\) masks, respectively; their deduplicated union has \(526429\)
members.  The \(4096\) A+ masks are disjoint from all three, giving \(530525\)
distinct necessary \(I_{18}\) clauses.  Because the common formula already
contains the universal family, the strengthened formula appends \(278754\)
new hitting clauses and the four retention units.  Its deterministic DIMACS
image has \(154190\) variables, \(997210\) clauses, \(390604816\) bytes, and
SHA-256
\[
 \sha{4f7e8f5b724a657888c7814d2c25cac41c283c3db356fb8f1a15f4c7322c375d}.
\]
An independent reconstruction agrees byte for byte.  This is strictly
stronger than A+: it installs the two families that were previously used
only as no-repeat filters and directly blocks the displayed A+ witness.  It
also differs from the deletion-first master with all fixed-base cuts, because
it retains the full edge formula and adds \(43614\) history-only masks plus
the \(4096\) A+ masks.  Formula construction alone is not a SAT or UNSAT
result.

We finally combined this complete mask bank with the full all-pair
maximal-triangle-free encoding of \cref{fin:prop:branch1-mtf-normal-form}.  The
resulting direct primary-graph CNF has \(639290\) variables, \(1972360\)
clauses, \(408370088\) bytes, and SHA-256
\[
 \sha{09e1784c3f43c4901dc6f6b4749fc5a74b025b08f74be58133edd1ed1096ebdb}.
\]
A separate reconstruction agreed byte for byte, both before and after a
command-line symlink-validation repair that did not change the formula.
Exactly one externally bounded Sirius call used CaDiCaL~3.0.1 at source
commit \sha{c60730422e758ef1cebe7aeddf2dda31c996bf04}, a \(300\)-second wall,
non-binary DRAT, and a \(10\)-GiB proof cap.  The wrapper exited \(124\), and
the result file contained exactly \texttt{c UNKNOWN}.  The run recorded
\(13347\) conflicts, \(105834\) decisions, and \(1216037481\) propagations;
these are resource telemetry only.  Its incomplete \(922038097\)-byte proof
prefix was hashed and deleted without replay.  Consequently the run produced
no model, certificate, learned cut, branch closure, or global Ramsey
implication.

Accordingly, none of the following is established: a repair with exactly
seven deletions; nonexistence of such a repair; the exact value of \(\rho(H)\);
or a \(100\)-vertex \((3,18)\)-Ramsey graph.  A machine-readable Boolean field
whose default value is false is likewise not evidence of nonexistence unless
the companion establishment flag and a checked proof support it.
